trust_decision.summary: Inbound gossipsub RPCs must have their control arrays bounded at the protobuf decode boundary AND at each control handler; the pinned commit enforces neither, because the limits object is keyed `control$` while the codec reads `limits.control`, the default limits are Infinity, and handleIHave/handleIWant hash every message id in the RPC.

landing_point.why: The advisory names IHAVE and IWANT control arrays, so an engineer looks first at the two loops that walk messageIDs (handleIHave 1319-1335, handleIWant 1385-1403). The real gate is ~450 lines earlier at the RPC.decode call (865-883), whose limits object never reaches the codec.

fix_sites.entry_point: every inbound gossipsub RPC (onIncomingStream:615 -> pipePeerReadStream:725); these defaults apply whenever GossipsubOpts.decodeRpcLimits is absent (gossipsub.ts:318)
inbound gossipsub stream handler registered at gossipsub.ts:469 (onIncomingStream:615 -> pipePeerReadStream:725)
same inbound stream path; new private decodeRpc() helper called at 865
start/stop lifecycle (stop:586), called by libp2p when the node stops
public heartbeat() (gossipsub.ts:2588) run on the heartbeat interval
inbound stream -> handleIHave/handleIWant, which read GossipsubMaxIHaveLength and the new GossipsubMaxIWantMessages

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The limits module holds only a type and its default values and the report is about IHAVE/IWANT handling, so setting a limit where the arrays are iterated looks sufficient.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: An honest peer may legitimately advertise up to GossipsubMaxIHaveLength (5000) ids in one IHAVE and must keep being served, and the new per-peer IWANT counter must be reset by every heartbeat so an honest peer that has used its budget is served on the next interval (the fix's own test asserts this). A cap keyed on GossipsubMaxIHaveMessages (10) or a counter that is never cleared breaks legitimate gossip.

O6_input_shapes: one IHAVE entry with many messageIDs (array nested in an entry)
one IWANT entry with many messageIDs
many control entries of one type (ihave/iwant/graft/prune/idontwant counts)
one PRUNE entry with many peers (nested repeated inside repeated)
one IDONTWANT entry with many messageIDs
many small IWANT RPCs from the same peer inside one heartbeat (rate, not size)
aggregate: maxControlMessages entries each carrying maxIhave/maxIwant ids
no options at all (default limits) versus a custom decodeRpcLimits
decode input as Uint8Array or Uint8ArrayList

O7_producer.where: packages/gossipsub/src/message/rpc.ts:1377-1412 (RPC codec builds subscriptions/messages/control from the wire and applies opts.limits?.control)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GRAFT control array: handleGraft walks every graft entry and answers with one PRUNE per unknown/backed-off/over-Dhi topic, then Promise.all(prune.map(makePrune)); there is no per-call or per-heartbeat cap in the handler at the pinned commit, and the fix bounds it only through the decode defaults.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names IHAVE and IWANT; GRAFT is a different control type and the new decode defaults already cap control entries at 5000.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Public handleReceivedRpc(from, rpc) accepts an already-decoded RPC and never passes through decodeRpcLimits, so a caller or overriding subclass can hand it arbitrarily large subscriptions, messages and control arrays.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is not part of the exported GossipSub interface and only the internal stream pipeline calls it, so no external caller can reach it.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, the public API surface above the private handlers

O8_uncovered_routes.route: decodeRpcLimits is taken wholesale (opts.decodeRpcLimits ?? defaultDecodeRpcLimits) with no merge over defaults, so a partial limits object leaves the omitted fields undefined, which protons treats as no limit.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: DecodeRPCLimits declares all seven fields required, so a TypeScript caller must pass every limit.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, constructor (configuration route), 1000 lines above the handlers

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Cap the peers processed by handlePrune/pxConnect per call, the way prune$ peers is capped at decode.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: prune.peers is the same nested repeated field as ihave.messageIDs and reaches per-peer signed-peer-record decoding and peerStore merges with no handler-side bound; a maintainer hardening PX would add it beside the existing IDONTWANT cap.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Add a processed-entry budget to handleGraft using the same `out:` labelled-loop idiom the fix adds to handleIHave.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: handleIdontwant already uses that exact labelled-break pattern (gossipsub.ts:1576-1588), so copying it into the remaining control handlers is the obvious next commit.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Merge caller-supplied partial limits over the defaults instead of replacing the whole object.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The limits arrive from user configuration (GossipsubOpts.decodeRpcLimits) where partial JSON objects are common; a maintainer could write {...defaultDecodeRpcLimits, ...opts.decodeRpcLimits}.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Give maxInboundDataLength a default so one length-prefixed frame cannot be unbounded.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The option is plumbed from gossipsub.ts:722 and has no default, so the same DoS shape arrives one layer earlier and a maintainer hardening this advisory would notice it.

O9_family: improper input validation leading to uncontrolled resource consumption (unbounded repeated protobuf arrays driving per-id CPU work)

O10_build.toolchain: yarn workspaces + aegir 47 (tsc build, mocha + chai tests, eslint); src/message/rpc.ts is generated by protons 8 and committed, so no codegen is needed to build
O10_build.project_tests: packages/gossipsub/test/*.spec.ts plus test/unit and test/e2e, run with `aegir test -t node -f dist/test/*.spec.js`; the gossipsub specs use in-memory mock muxers and a MemoryDatastore (test/utils/create-pubsub.ts:190-300) and run offline; test/e2e/go-gossipsub.spec.ts needs a go-libp2p binary/Docker and is not part of this area

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Slice each entry's messageIDs to GossipsubMaxIHaveLength inside handleIHave/handleIWant and stop there, leaving the `control$` limits key that the codec never reads and the Infinity defaults in place.

out_of_scope_notes: packages/floodsub has its own generated codec with the same ihave/iwant/prune arrays (packages/floodsub/src/message/rpc.ts) decoded with no limits via pbStream (packages/floodsub/src/peer-streams.ts:42) and never processes control messages; it is a separate pubsub implementation outside this gossipsub advisory and was not pursued.

InboundStream passes maxInboundDataLength straight through (packages/gossipsub/src/gossipsub.ts:722, packages/gossipsub/src/stream.ts:72) and the option has no default, so a single frame is unbounded at the pinned commit; that is a frame-size sink rather than the control-array sink this advisory's fix covers.
unverified: Repo size in MB could not be measured without shell access, so repo_mb is null; the monorepo contains ~50 packages under packages/ and interop/.
present_in_latest is unknown for all three O8 routes: the inputs give no latest release and no latest tree was available to inspect.

handleReceivedRpc is public on the GossipSub class (gossipsub.ts:928) but is absent from the exported GossipSub interface (packages/gossipsub/src/index.ts:290-398); it was counted as a second entry point because the code comments call it the RPC-handling override point.

O4 distance is logical (decode layer versus handler layer), not physical: all nine fix sites are inside packages/gossipsub, with 3 files between the landing point and message/decodeRpc.ts and 0 package boundaries.

Buildability was judged from package.json and the workspace manifests only; no build, install or test was run, and dependency installation is assumed to be possible offline from a prepared node_modules.
